1.title: ORBIT #001: Great Blue Hole
1.text:
This circular hole is three hundred eighteen meters wide, and no one dug it.

The Great Blue Hole is a three hundred eighteen meter wide marine sinkhole off Belize, formed when sea levels fell during the Quaternary. Jacques Cousteau made it famous as a top scuba diving site. Imagery: Esri, Maxar, Earthstar Geographics. Photos: Jesse Allen; jayhem, CC BY 2.0, Wikimedia Commons. Source: Wikipedia.

2.title: ORBIT #002: Vredefort Dome
2.text:
One hundred ten kilometers of hills, and they all circle one small town.

The Vredefort Dome in South Africa is the central uplift of an impact structure formed about 2.023 billion years ago, whose worn-away crater was estimated at 170 to 300 km across. It was added to UNESCO's World Heritage list in 2005. Imagery: Esri, Maxar, Earthstar Geographics. Photos: Júlio Reis (User:Tintazul), Wikimedia Commons. Source: Wikipedia.

3.title: ORBIT #003: Racetrack Playa
3.text:
Rocks up to three hundred twenty kilograms crawl across this dry lake, leaving tracks.

Racetrack Playa is a dry lake in Death Valley National Park, California, where sailing stones weighing up to 320 kg travel across the clay and leave linear tracks. The phenomenon has been documented since 1948. Imagery: Esri, Maxar, Earthstar Geographics. Photos: Dan Duriscoe, for the en:U.S. National P; Lgcharlot, CC BY-SA 4.0, Wikimedia Commons. Source: Wikipedia.

4.title: ORBIT #004: Nazca Lines
4.text:
Who scratched over eight hundred miles of lines into this desert?

The Nazca lines are geoglyphs in the soil of the Nazca Desert in southern Peru, made between 500 BC and 500 AD by removing reddish-brown pebbles to expose lighter subsoil. Their combined length is more than 1,300 km, and drones have found several hundred new figures this century. Imagery: Esri, Maxar, Earthstar Geographics. Photos: Diego Delso, CC BY-SA 4.0, Wikimedia Commons. Source: Wikipedia.

5.title: ORBIT #005: Area 51
5.text:
You can zoom onto this airfield. The CIA confirmed it in two thousand thirteen.

Area 51 is a highly classified US Air Force facility in southern Nevada, officially called Homey Airport or Groom Lake. The USAF and CIA acquired it in 1955 mainly for Lockheed U-2 flight tests, and the CIA publicly acknowledged it in 2013. Imagery: Esri, Maxar, Earthstar Geographics. Photos: Doc Searls from Santa Barbara, USA, CC BY 2.0; Geckow; Jimderkaisser, CC BY-SA 3.0, Wikimedia Commons. Source: Wikipedia.

6.title: ORBIT #006: Lake Hillier
6.text:
Six hundred meters of pink water, and the ocean is just past the sand.

Lake Hillier is a saline lake about 600 metres long on Middle Island, off the south coast of Western Australia, and its pink colour stays the same even in a container. The colour is believed to come from the organism Dunaliella salina, which the Extreme Microbiome Project found in a metagenomic analysis of the lake. Imagery: Esri, Maxar, Earthstar Geographics. Photos: Aussie Oc, CC BY-SA 4.0; Yodaobione, CC BY-SA 4.0, Wikimedia Commons. Source: Wikipedia.

7.title: ORBIT #007: Danakil Depression
7.text:
A valley two hundred kilometers long, and its floor sits below sea level.

The Danakil Depression is a valley about 200 by 50 km across Ethiopia and Eritrea, about 125 m below sea level and the third lowest place in Africa. It is a rift that began about 11 million years ago, as the Danakil microplate rotated and pulled away from the Nubian plate. Imagery: Esri, Maxar, Earthstar Geographics. Photos: Yonas Kidane, CC BY-SA 2.0, Wikimedia Commons. Source: Wikipedia.

8.title: ORBIT #008: Dallol
8.text:
Green acid ponds and yellow crust, with a pH below one.

Dallol is a hydrothermal system around a cinder cone volcano in Ethiopia's Danakil Depression, with green acid ponds below pH one. Its Afar name means dissolution or disintegration, and iron gives its ground yellow and brown colors. Imagery: Esri, Maxar, Earthstar Geographics. Photos: Hervé Sthioul, CC BY 2.5; Ji-Elle, CC BY-SA 3.0, Wikimedia Commons. Source: Wikipedia.

9.title: ORBIT #009: Socotra
9.text:
One in three plants on this island grows nowhere else on Earth.

Socotra is a Yemeni island in the Indian Ocean, and a third of its plant life is found nowhere else on Earth. Geographically it belongs to Africa, and in 2008 it became a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Imagery: Esri, Maxar, Earthstar Geographics. Photos: Boris Khvostichenko(User:Boriskhv), CC BY-SA 4.0; Email4mobile, Wikimedia Commons. Source: Wikipedia.

10.title: ORBIT #010: North Sentinel Island
10.text:
Why may no boat come within three miles of this island?

North Sentinel Island in India's Andaman Islands is home to the Sentinelese, an uncontacted indigenous tribe. A 1956 regulation bans travel there and any approach closer than five kilometers, to protect them from mainland infectious diseases. Imagery: Esri, Maxar, Earthstar Geographics. Photos: PJeganathan, CC BY-SA 4.0, Wikimedia Commons. Source: Wikipedia.
